verdict.rationale: Airbyte's architecture inherently supports data portability: it is open-source (Core, self-hostable via Docker/abctl/Kubernetes), writes synced data into standard destinations you own (warehouses, lakes, databases) with one-to-one table mapping rather than a proprietary internal format, and exposes PyAirbyte/API for programmatic access to extracted data. However there is no explicit documented 'export and leave' workflow, and community evidence notes Airbyte is not fully open-source in practice (freemium model gating some features like SSO/RBAC behind paid tiers), which tempers the openness claim. Missing for 10: an explicit data-export/migration guide, independent confirmation that self-hosted users can fully migrate without lock-in, and resolution of the freemium/open-source tension.
